tagline: Prom Country's wild coast, Strzelecki rainforest and coal-mining heritage
description: South Gippsland, also known as Prom Country, takes in the southernmost point of the Australian mainland. Its draws range from coastal parks and beaches to mountain rainforest and maritime and coal-mining heritage. The State Coal Mine at Wonthaggi worked from 1910 to 1968 and is now a Parks Victoria heritage area with a cafe. The Prom Country Information Centre at Korumburra is about 90 minutes' drive from Melbourne.
whyVisit: Walk wild coastal parks and beaches
Explore coal-mining heritage
Cycle the Great Southern Rail Trail

goodToKnow.title: Drive, don't rely on buses
goodToKnow.detail: V/Line's daily bus runs only from Melbourne to Yarram, so reaching the coastal parks and towns is realistic only by car.

goodToKnow.title: Stop at the info centre
goodToKnow.detail: The Prom Country Information Centre on the South Gippsland Highway at Korumburra is the region's main visitor centre.

bestTimeBlurb: Beaches, coastal walks and rail-trail rides are at their best in {months}.
notes: Best months inferred from the coastal and outdoor focus. No seasonal tags.

tagline: Hanging Rock, Mount Macedon and village gardens between Melbourne and Bendigo
description: The Macedon Ranges is a region of native forest, villages and cool-climate gardens in Central Victoria. Hanging Rock, a 718 m volcanic mamelon formed 6.25 million years ago, was the setting of Joan Lindsay's novel Picnic at Hanging Rock. Mount Macedon's Camel's Hump reaches 1,001 m, the region's highest point, and snow falls there on 15 to 20 days a year. The region has more working artists per capita than anywhere else in Victoria.
whyVisit: Hike volcanic rock at Hanging Rock
Wander historic villages and markets
Visit cool-climate gardens and lookouts

goodToKnow.title: Colder than Melbourne
goodToKnow.detail: Mount Macedon sits above 1,000 m and sees snow most winters. Pack a layer even when the city is mild.

goodToKnow.title: Drive between villages
goodToKnow.detail: Towns and sights are spread across about 1,750 sq km, so a car is the practical way to link villages, gardens and Hanging Rock.

goodToKnow.title: Check garden opening dates
goodToKnow.detail: Open gardens and peony picking run on set seasons and dates. Check the regional tourism site before you go.

bestTimeBlurb: Milder {months} suit hiking and gardens, away from the hotter summers and colder winters.
notes: Best months are an inference from climate facts. Garden and peony dates not found. 'Snow most winters' in a tip follows the researcher's wording; the sourced fact is snow on 15-20 days a year.

tagline: Regional Wimmera River city and gateway to the Silo Art Trail and Mount Arapiles
description: Horsham is a regional city on a bend in the Wimmera River, about 300 km north-west of Melbourne, and the most populous city in the Wimmera. It is the gateway to the Silo Art Trail and the north-western side of the Grampians National Park. Mount Arapiles, about 30 minutes' drive west, rises about 140 m above the plains and is one of Australia's premier rock-climbing sites. In town, the Regional Art Gallery, the Botanic Gardens and the riverside fill a stopover on the Western Highway.
whyVisit: Rock climb on the Wimmera plains
Follow the Silo Art Trail

goodToKnow.title: Bring water to Arapiles
goodToKnow.detail: Tank water at the Mount Arapiles campground is not for drinking, so bring your own and plenty of it.

goodToKnow.title: Summer heat
goodToKnow.detail: Horsham sees about 25 extreme-heat days a year and January averages a 30.6C maximum, so plan outdoor time for cooler months.

bestTimeBlurb: Summers are hot with frequent extreme heat, so {months} are the mild months to visit.
notes: Best months inferred from climate text. Silo art spots are not described in the research record beyond the trail itself. The Arapiles reason avoids naming the spot (general rock climbing).

tagline: Great Ocean Road beach town with a 3 km main beach and Otway waterfalls nearby
description: Lorne is a Great Ocean Road town 138 km, about two hours, from Melbourne, which began as a logging town. Its main beach runs about 3 km for bathing and surfing, and a pier is used for fishing. Cafes and galleries line Mountjoy Parade, and the town borders Great Otway National Park. The Lorne to Apollo Bay section of the road was finished in November 1932.
whyVisit: Swim and surf off a long beach
Chase waterfalls through Otway fern gullies
Drive the Great Ocean Road coast

goodToKnow.title: New Year weekend crowds
goodToKnow.detail: Over 20,000 people visit on the first weekend of January for the Pier to Pub swim, so book ahead and expect crowds.

goodToKnow.title: Steep road to Teddy's Lookout
goodToKnow.detail: The road up to Teddy's Lookout at the end of George Street is steep, so drive carefully.

goodToKnow.title: Summer fills the town
goodToKnow.detail: Holiday-makers fill Lorne every summer, so arrive early in the day or visit outside school holidays.

bestTimeBlurb: Mild {months} weather suits beach time, though summer is busy and March is quieter.
notes: Best months are an editorial inference from the mild-summer climate.

tagline: Granite tors, snow gums and sheer cliffs on a plateau that tops out at 1,723 m
description: Mount Buffalo National Park covers 31,000 ha about 350 km north-east of Melbourne, and was reserved on 4 November 1898, making it one of Australia's oldest national parks. The plateau has granite boulders and rock formations, sheer cliffs, waterfalls and snow gum woodland, and reaches 1,723 m at The Horn. The Chalet, built in 1910, overlooks sheets of granite and the Ovens and Buckland valleys. Bogong moths shelter in the rock crevices at The Horn, and birds feed on them.
whyVisit: Walk granite tors and plateau lookouts
See wildflowers across the plateau
Play in the snow in winter

goodToKnow.title: Carry snow chains
goodToKnow.detail: Snow chains must be carried every day, for all vehicles including 4WDs, and fitted where road signs say so. Penalties apply.

goodToKnow.title: Stay in Bright or Porepunkah
goodToKnow.detail: There is no accommodation at the Chalet. Visitors stay in the nearby towns of Porepunkah and Bright.

goodToKnow.title: Snow play and skiing risks
goodToKnow.detail: Dingo Dell and Cresta Valley suit beginners for tobogganing and snow play. Back-country skiing carries avalanche and weather risks.

bestTimeBlurb: Wildflowers bloom on the plateau's grassy plains in {months}, and winter brings snow play.
notes: Winter snow season months are not sourced, so no seasonal tag was written. Lake Catani camping not used as a reason.

tagline: Gold-rush streets, Ned Kelly history and a cool-climate town on a rail trail
description: Beechworth was a gold-producing region and centre of government between 1852 and 1857, and its well-preserved historic precinct includes the Court House and Burke Museum. Ned Kelly spent time in HM Prison Beechworth, and courthouse displays tell the story. The town sits at 560 m, about 284 km from Melbourne, and is one end of the Murray to the Mountains Rail Trail. Waterfalls, Spring Creek Gorge, the Beechworth Bakery, a brewery and wineries round out a stay.
whyVisit: Walk gold-rush streets and heritage buildings
Follow Ned Kelly's trail
Cycle a paved rail trail

goodToKnow.title: Bring your own car
goodToKnow.detail: There is no car hire in Beechworth, so arrive with a vehicle or plan to walk the compact historic centre.

goodToKnow.title: Hire bikes for the rail trail
goodToKnow.detail: The old railway line to Wangaratta and Bright is a paved rail trail, and bicycles can be hired in town.

goodToKnow.title: Festival weekend crowds
goodToKnow.detail: The Golden Horseshoes Festival parade at Easter and the August Ned Kelly Weekend bring crowds, so book stays early.

bestTimeBlurb: Mild {months} weather suits walking and cycling in a town that is cool for much of the year.
notes: Best months are an inference from the 560 m climate. Festival tip is a tip, not a reason or spot.

tagline: Murray River city of paddle steamers, grapes and citrus groves in the Sunraysia
description: Mildura is a regional city on the Victorian bank of the Murray River and the largest settlement in Sunraysia. George Chaffey founded the irrigation settlement in 1887, and the area now grows about 80% of Victoria's grapes and more than 70% of Australia's dried vine fruits, plus citrus, avocados and almonds. Paddle steamers pass through the lock and weir at Lock 11, and the Murray can be cruised on the Paddlesteamer Melbourne or a chartered houseboat. Mungo National Park is about two hours away for a day trip.
whyVisit: Cruise the Murray by paddlesteamer
Taste fresh Sunraysia produce
Swim and walk along the river

goodToKnow.title: Fruit fly zone
goodToKnow.detail: Don't bring fruit or vegetables into Mildura's fruit-fly-free zone, or take them out across the zone or interstate borders. Fines can reach $100,000.

goodToKnow.title: Hire a car
goodToKnow.detail: Most attractions need a car. Local buses run on weekdays in business hours, and rental companies operate from the airport.

bestTimeBlurb: Summers average 32C with some days over 40C, so {months} are milder for river walks.
notes: Best months inferred from climate text. Wine not claimed as the research gives grapes and dried fruit only. Inland beach claim (billed as Victoria's largest) left out of copy.

tagline: Mountain ash forest, scenic drives and Melbourne's nearest winter snowplay
description: Yarra Ranges National Park, created in December 1995, covers 76,003 ha of wet mountain ash forest and cool temperate rainforest in the Great Dividing Range. Mountain ash is the world's tallest flowering tree. Mount Donna Buang (1,245 m) has a 21 m lookout tower with views over Melbourne, the Yarra Valley and the Dandenong and Cathedral Ranges, and near Warburton the Rainforest Gallery is a viewing platform 15 m above the forest floor. About 84% of the park is a water supply catchment closed to the public.
whyVisit: Walk among the world's tallest flowering trees
Drive winding mountain ash forest roads
See Melbourne's nearest snow in winter

goodToKnow.title: Most of the park is closed
goodToKnow.detail: Most of the park protects Melbourne's drinking water and is closed to visitors. Stay on signed tracks and roads.

goodToKnow.title: No facilities in the park
goodToKnow.detail: There are no shops or services inside the park. Stock up in Healesville, Marysville or Warburton.

bestTimeBlurb: Warm {months} days suit forest walks and drives, and Jun–Aug brings snow to Mount Donna Buang.
notes: Best months editorial. Snow cover varies by year. Black Spur and Lady Talbot Drive are the sourced basis for the drives reason.
